# Synthetic transcript fixtures

Generated by `generate.py` from one fictional doctor–patient conversation (colorectal biopsy
results). No real patients, no real vendor output. Shapes follow the vendors' public docs as
of 2026-11: they encode *our reading* of the docs, so a parser passing them is not proof it
handles real output. Replace or supplement with real outputs when available (issue #19).

Regenerate after editing the generator: `python tests/fixtures/transcripts/generate.py`
(`tests/test_transcript_fixtures.py` fails if the committed files are stale).

| File | Shape | Expected importer result |
|---|---|---|
| `deepgram_utterances.json` | Deepgram pre-recorded, `diarize` + `utterances` | import |
| `deepgram_words_only.json` | Deepgram, `diarize` only (group words by speaker) | import |
| `deepgram_multichannel.json` | Deepgram `multichannel`, no diarization | import, speakers `ch0`/`ch1` |
| `aws_audio_segments.json` | AWS Transcribe, current layout with `audio_segments` | import |
| `aws_items_speaker_label.json` | AWS, `speaker_label` on items, no `audio_segments` | import |
| `aws_legacy_speaker_segments.json` | AWS, speakers only in `speaker_labels.segments` | import (match by time) |
| `aws_channel_identification.json` | AWS channel identification (`channel_labels`) | import, speakers `ch_0`/`ch_1` |
| `aws_medical.json` | AWS Transcribe Medical conversation | import |
| `whisperx.json` | WhisperX with diarization; digits have no timing/speaker | import |
| `whisperx_unknown_speaker.json` | WhisperX, one segment without speaker | import + `unknown` warning |
| `openai_diarized.json` | OpenAI `diarized_json` (field names unverified) | import, no confidences |
| `deepgram_spanish.json` | Deepgram, `detected_language: es` | import + language warning |
| `deepgram_single_speaker.json` | Deepgram, one speaker (dictation) | import + one-speaker warning |
| `whisper_plain.json` | openai-whisper, no speakers | 422 `undiarized_transcript` |
| `aws_call_analytics.json` | AWS Call Analytics | 422 `unsupported_transcript_format` |
| `aws_healthscribe.json` | AWS HealthScribe | 422 `unsupported_transcript_format` |
| `deepgram_empty.json` | Deepgram, no words | 422 `empty_transcript` |
| `truncated.json` | cut-off JSON | 422 `invalid_json` |

Low-confidence words (for ASR-error reporting): `adenocarcinoma` 0.41, `sigmoid` 0.55,
`mismatch` 0.58. AWS fixtures carry a fake `jobName` containing `SYNTHETIC-PATIENT-NAME`;
the importer must never echo it. Empty and non-UTF-8 uploads and oversized files are built
inside the tests, not stored here.

## Sample conversations

`scenarios.py` holds nine more scripted conversations (one per pathology scenario, rotating
vendors) with an answer key per doctor statement. `generate.py` also renders them to
`frontend/public/transcripts/<folder>/<id>.json` plus `index.json` (the UI's sample panel) and
writes the keys to `backend/evals/factcheck/keys/` (see `backend/evals/factcheck/README.md`).
Each scenario has its own low-confidence word map and timing seed, and one planted
speech-to-text error in a doctor line (`asr_error`, e.g. "colin" for "colon"), scored low only at
that spot. The generator also writes per-sentence triage gold labels to `backend/evals/triage/keys/`
(see `backend/evals/triage/README.md`) and the saved imports in
`frontend/src/mocks/review/__fixtures__/` that the mock reviews are tested against. Synthetic and
AI-written. `tests/test_transcript_samples.py` and `tests/test_triage_gold.py` check that they are up to
date, import cleanly and label every doctor sentence.
